memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Sukkoth. There were about six hundred
thousand men on foot, besides women and children. Many other people went up with
them, and also large droves of livestock, both flocks and herds."
- Ex 12:37-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
They walked out. After four hundred and thirty years, they walked out.

Two things in these verses deserve notice. First, the size. Six hundred thousand
men on foot, besides women and children. A nation, not a village. God had said
to Abraham, "I will make you into a great nation" (Gen 12:2), when Abraham had
no children at all.

Second, and easy to miss: "Many other people went up with them." Egyptians and
others joined the exodus. They had seen what the God of Israel had done, and
they threw in their lot with His people.

This is the first hint of something that runs right through the Bible. God's
salvation was never fenced off. Rahab, Ruth, the Ninevites who repented, the
Roman centurion, the Ethiopian official. Right at the birth of the nation, the
crowd was already mixed.

To be honest, this mixed multitude would later cause trouble, stirring up
craving in the wilderness (Num 11:4). Being among God's people is not the same
as belonging to God. But the door was open, and it still is. Revelation shows a
crowd "from every nation, tribe, people and language" (Rev 7:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you belong to God, or only travel among His people?
2. Who might come with you if you spoke about what God has done?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You gather people from everywhere. Let my life draw others
to come along, and keep my own heart truly Yours. Amen.
